n: Sec. 6.4.9 states that once the Architect has completed the Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase (equivalent to 90% of his work), he is entitled to ninety percent (90%) of the Architect's fee if the Owner fails to implement the plans.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.9

q: A Group I (Simple) project has a PCC of only P45,000,000, which falls within the '50M and less' bracket (flat percentage, no base amount). Under the DAEDS schedule (5% flat), what is the RPF?
n: For PCC of 50M and less, Group I DAEDS RPF is a flat 5% of PCC: 0.05 x 45M = P2,250,000.00.  Source: SPP Doc. 202, Building Type Group I (DAEDS) fee schedule

q: Under Sec. 11.3.1, the Architect acting as Project Manager for Comprehensive Architectural Services is entitled to what RPF, as a percentage of PCC?
n: Sec. 11.3.1 states the RPF for Project Manager is 2% to 5% of Project Construction Cost (PCC).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 11.3.1

q: For a project handled under DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services), what percentage of the corresponding DAEDS professional fee does the architectural design services portion constitute?
n: Sec. 4.1.1.5 states the architectural design services shall constitute sixty percent (60%) of the corresponding stated professional fee (PF) for DAEDS for the project.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.5

q: Group VI ('Repetitive Construction, Except Housing') applies to a project when:
o: the client requests a 50% discount on the second building
the same architect is re-hired for a second unrelated project
the project is built in phases over several years
the plans/designs and related Contract Documents are re-used without amendments to the drawings and specifications
n: Group VI applies specifically when plans/designs and related Contract Documents are reused without amendment to the drawings and specifications — i.e., true repetitive construction, not merely repeat clientele.  Source: SPP Doc. 202, Building Type Group VI

q: Continuing that scenario, upon completion of the Contract Document Phase, cumulative payments should reach 90% of the PF. How much ADDITIONAL payment is due at that stage (from the prior 40% cumulative)?
n: Cumulative target = 90% x P5,000,000 = P4,500,000; already paid (40%) = P2,000,000; additional due = P4,500,000 - P2,000,000 = P2,500,000, matching the 50% increment in Sec. 6.4.4.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.4.4
scenario: Scenario: A Client and Architect agree on a total Professional Fee (PF) of P5,000,000 for Regular Design Services, to be paid per the Sec. 6.4 cumulative payment schedule (5% / 20% / 40% / 90% / 90% / 100% cumulative).

q: The Retainer method of compensation (Sec. 4.3.13) is best described as:
o: A stipulated amount paid at regular intervals ensuring the PCA's availability, with additional services billed separately
A method that can never include per diem or hourly add-ons
A method exclusively used for expert witness testimony
A one-time lump sum paid only at project completion
n: Sec. 4.3.13.1 describes the retainer as a stipulated amount paid at regular intervals to ensure availability of the PCA's services, covering minimum required services, with all additional services paid separately.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.13.1

q: Under which PRBoA issuance was this Architect's Guidelines document (Annex A) approved, adopted and promulgated in 2016?
n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture approved, adopted and promulgated the Architect's Guidelines through PRBoA Resolution No. 06, Series of 2016, published in the Official Gazette (Vol. 112, No. 38, Sept. 19, 2016).  Source: PRBoA Resolution No. 06, s. 2016

q: What is the HIGHEST reasonable Recommended Professional Fee under this range?
n: At the high end of the 10%-15% range: 15% x P6,000,000 = P900,000.00.  Source: SPP Doc. 203, Specialized Architectural Services fee schedule
scenario: Continuing the same Acoustic Design engagement (Cost of Work = P6,000,000, RPF range 10%-15%).

q: Under Sec. 13.6.9, in a Project ADC, if no contract is signed within how many months of the Jury's award announcement, is the first prize winner entitled to an additional sum equal to the first prize?
n: Sec. 13.6.9 states the first prize winner receives a further sum equal to the first prize if no contract is signed within twelve (12) months of the announcement of the Jury's award.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.6.9

q: A built-in cabinetry and architectural interiors project (Group 8) has a PCC of P5,000,000. What is the Architect's RPF?
n: Group 8 RPF = 15% x P5,000,000 = P750,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.8 (Group 8)
scenario: Scenario: A project involving extensive detail (built-in components, special fittings, and architectural interiors, Group 8 classification) has a Project Construction Cost of P5,000,000.

q: Under Sec. 12.2.2.2, whatever mode of construction involvement the Architect adopts under Design-Build Services, he/she must strictly adhere to the tenets of which document?
n: Sec. 12.2.2.2 requires strict adherence to the tenets of the Architects Credo, including disclosure of any conflict-of-interest business investment or venture.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 12.2.2.2

q: Within how many calendar days from submission of the statement of account must the Client make progress payments for Pre-Design Services, upon the Architect's request?
n: Sec. 5.3 states the Client shall make progress payments upon request of the Architect within seven (7) calendar days from submission of the statement of account.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 5.3

q: Besides Man-months x Multiplier and MDPE, which of the following is listed among the 'Other Specialized Architectural Services' compensation methods (distinct from the main AI/Acoustic/Lighting/SDP percentage method)?
o: Rate Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses
n: The 'Other Specialized Architectural Services' list includes: Man-months x Multiplier, MDPE, Per Diem + Reimbursable Expenses, Retainer + Reimbursable Expenses, and Rate Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses.  Source: SPP Doc. 203, Specialized Architectural Services — Methods of Compensation

q: Which of the following building types is classified under Group 1 (simplest utilization/character) in Sec. 6.3.1?
n: Group 1 lists buildings of the simplest utilization and character requiring minimal architectural finishes, including armories, bakeries, hangars, parking structures, and warehouses.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1

q: A Group II (Moderate) project — a hospital-adjacent office building — has a PCC of P650,000,000, falling in the '500M–1B' bracket (RPF = 18.5M + 2% of excess of 500M). What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee?
n: RPF = 18.5M + [0.02 x (650M - 500M)] = 18.5M + (0.02 x 150M) = 18.5M + 3M = P21,500,000.00.  Source: SPP Doc. 202, Building Type Group II (DAEDS) fee schedule

q: A Group III (Exceptional) project — a hotel — has a PCC of P300,000,000, falling in the '200M–500M' bracket (RPF = 11.5M + 4% of excess of 200M). What is the DAEDS Recommended Professional Fee?
n: RPF = 11.5M + [0.04 x (300M - 200M)] = 11.5M + (0.04 x 100M) = 11.5M + 4M = P15,500,000.00.  Source: SPP Doc. 202, Building Type Group III (DAEDS) fee schedule

q: Under Time-based fees (Sec. 4.3), which of the following is NOT listed as a typical use case?
o: Services which are not well defined
Full-blown DAEDS services for a P1 billion mixed-use tower
n: Sec. 4.3.2 lists undefined/partial/additional services, pre-design services, and expert-witness/specialist consultancy work as typical time-based engagements — not large, fully defined DAEDS contracts, which are typically percentage-based.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.3.2

q: A Client wants cost certainty from the outset and both parties can clearly and fully define the scope of services at the start of the project. Which method of compensation, per Sec. 4.2.1, is most appropriate?
n: Sec. 4.2.1 states Lump Sum/Fixed Fee 'may be used when the scope of services required can be clearly and fully defined at the outset of the project.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.2.1

q: Per Annex A, 'Cost of Work (CoW)' is used specifically for which category of projects?
o: Architectural interiors, acoustics, lighting works, site development, and landscaping under Specialized Architectural Services
n: Annex A defines Cost of Work as the total cost of fixtures/accessories for architectural interiors, acoustics, lighting, site development/landscaping designed by the Specialist Architect/SCs — used for Specialized Architectural Services projects.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Cost of Work)

q: Which incentive-type contract, under Sec. 9.2.2.3, pays the Construction Manager a fee that is unaffected by variations between estimate and bids, unless the Owner increases scope?
n: Sec. 9.2.2.3 (Firm Fixed Price) states the Owner pays a fixed fee unaffected by variations between the estimate and bids or by change orders, unless the Owner initiates a scope increase.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 9.2.2.3

q: Per Annex A, 'Project Development Cost' includes construction cost, professional fees, permits, clearances/utilities, and additionally which of the following?
o: Cost of acquiring the project site/lot and cost of money
The BSP prevailing interest rate on late payments
n: Annex A defines Project Development Cost as including construction cost, all professional fees, permits, clearances and utilities, cost of acquiring the project site/lot, and cost of money.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex A (Project Development Cost)

q: A project's Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) professional fee is computed at P10,000,000. If the Owner instead contracts the Architect under DADS (engaging engineers separately), what is the Architect's DADS-equivalent architectural fee share?
n: Per Sec. 4.1.1.5, the architectural design services constitute 60% of the stated DAEDS professional fee: 60% x P10,000,000 = P6,000,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.5
scenario: Scenario: A commercial office project has a computed Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) professional fee of P10,000,000.

q: Using the same Group 1 warehouse project, if instead contracted under DADS ('Over P50.0M to P100.0M: P1,500,000 plus 2.4% of excess of P50.0M'), what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
n: Excess over P50M = P30M; 2.4% x P30M = P720,000; RPF = P1,500,000 + P720,000 = P2,220,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.1 (Group 1 DADS Fee Table)
scenario: Scenario: A Group 1 warehouse (simplest utilization/character building) has a Project Construction Cost of P80,000,000, and is contracted under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS).

q: Under the Percentage-based Fee method, the Professional Fee (PF) of the Architect is determined by:
o: Adding a fixed multiplier of 2.5 to the PCC
Dividing the PCC by the number of design phases
Multiplying floor area by the Architect's hourly rate
Multiplying the specified percentage times the Project Construction Cost (PCC)
n: Sec. 4.1.1.2 states the PF is determined by multiplying the specified percentage times the estimated, awarded, or final Project Construction Cost (PCC).  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 4.1.1.2

q: Continuing that scenario, what is the TOTAL fee for all 15 units (the 10-unit fee of P2,750,000 plus the remaining 5 units at 40% of RPF each, per the 11-30 unit bracket)?
n: Additional fee for units 11-15 (5 units) = 5 x 40% x P500,000 = 5 x P200,000 = P1,000,000. Total = P2,750,000 + P1,000,000 = P3,750,000.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 6.3.7 (Group 7 Housing Project schedule)
scenario: Scenario: A Client commissions a Housing Project of 15 identical single-detached units built from one set of plans/design (Group 7 classification), contracted under DAEDS. The Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for one unit alone is P500,000.

q: Per Annex B (Acronyms), what does 'RPF' stand for?
n: Annex B lists RPF as 'Recommended Professional Fee.'  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Annex B (Acronyms)

q: Under Sec. 7.3.2.1, what is the Recommended Professional Fee for Physical Planning of building sites, per hectare, for the first five (5) hectares?
n: Sec. 7.3.2.1 states the RPF is P50,000.00 per hectare for the first five (5) hectares net to the Architect.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 7.3.2.1

q: Per Sec. 3 (Criteria), the Architect's compensation should be based on mutual evaluation of which of the following?
o: Only the Architect's years in practice
The amount of the Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, effort and time required by the project
n: Section 3 states the criteria for computing compensation is based on mutual evaluation of the Architect's/firm's talents, skill, experience, effort, and time available for and required by the project.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 3 (Criteria)

q: Per Sec. 13.6.4, within what period must the Owner pay the prizes allotted after the official announcement of ADC results?
n: Sec. 13.6.4 states the Owner undertakes to pay the prizes allotted within one (1) month of the official announcement of the ADC results.  Source: Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 13.6.4

q: For the SAME project, the Group V DADS RPF is a flat 7.5% of PCC. What is the RPF under DADS?
n: Group V DADS RPF = 7.5% of PCC = 0.075 x P6,000,000 = P450,000.00.  Source: SPP Doc. 202, Building Type Group V (Monumental) fee schedule
scenario: A Group V (Monumental) project — a public memorial — has a PCC of P6,000,000.
